use /lib
from ../project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from ../prompt-mode import PromptEditor
from ../prompt-mode/chat-input import ChatInputScope
from ../editor import EditorScope
from ../palette import PaletteScope

export scope MainWindowScope:
    concept: {MainWindowConcept}

concept MainWindowConcept:
    pitch:
        The main window of the application allowing you interact with all main
        functionality.

    shape: {MainWindowShape}

shape MainWindowShape:
    description:
        Maximized window.

    darkMode:
        The whole window, including popups and notifications, supports a light
        and a dark theme.

        A "Dark mode" switch at the far right of the toolbar toggles between the
        two.

        The choice is persistent: it is saved for the user, across all
        projects, and restored on the next launch. Until a choice has been
        made, the window follows the operating system's light or dark
        appearance.

    escape:
        Pressing Esc anywhere in the window, including in an @{EditorScope}, moves
        focus to the @{ChatInputScope}. Esc first closes whatever it would
        otherwise dismiss, such as a completion menu or a popup.

    quitting:
        Quitting while the harness is working on a task or a question, or
        while a build is running, asks first. That goes for Ctrl+Q (Cmd+Q on
        macOS), Quit in the @{PaletteScope}, and the window's close button. The
        message is titled "Quit while a task is running?" and says what is
        still running. "Quit" exits, and "Keep Running" or Esc dismisses it.
        Asking to quit again while it is open doesn't open a second one, and an
        open palette closes first. Prompts waiting in the queue don't count as
        running work, since they are saved with the project.

    palette:
        Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on macOS) opens the @{PaletteScope} over the window, for
        fuzzy searching the project's files, the application's own commands,
        and the harness's commands, skills, and agents.

    header:
        toolbar:
            Toolbar on top that contains a button for @{ProjectDirectoryScope}
            As well as a Build button that will run `piton build`, with the
            "Dark mode" switch at the far right. There is no raw output view
            and no toggle for one.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='spec/scope/application/MainWindow.pi'; s=open(p).read()
pairs=[
('''        A "Dark mode" switch at the far right of the toolbar toggles between the
        two.''','''        A "Dark mode" switch in the ribbon's Application tab toggles between
        the two.'''),
('''    header:
        toolbar:
            Toolbar on top that contains a button for @{ProjectDirectoryScope}
            As well as a Build button that will run `piton build`, with the
            "Dark mode" switch at the far right. There is no raw output view
            and no toggle for one.
''','''    header:
        ribbon:
            overview:
                A ribbon runs along the top of the window, using gpui-kit's Tab
                component with its default styling. Its tabs are, in order:
                Project, Code, Spec, Research, and Application. The window
                always opens on Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's
                commands sit in groups. There is no raw output view and no
                toggle for one.

            groups:
                Each group has its title in small, muted text centred along its
                bottom, naming what its commands have in common. Groups sit
                side by side, with a thin vertical divider between each.

                project:
                    A "Project" group holds the button for the
                    @{ProjectDirectoryScope}.

                code:
                    Nothing yet.

                spec:
                    A "Build" group holds "Build Spec", which runs
                    `piton build`.

                research:
                    Nothing yet.

                application:
                    An "Appearance" group holds the "Dark mode" switch, and a
                    "Preferences" group holds "Settings", which opens the
                    settings window.

                A tab with no commands reads "No commands yet".

            commands:
                A command button shows a large icon above its label: a folder
                for the project, a hammer for Build Spec, and a gear for
                Settings. The project button reads "Open Project…" until a
                project is open, then the project's name. An on or off setting,
                like dark mode, is a switch rather than a button.

                A command's tooltip explains what it does rather than repeating
                its label, and gives its keyboard shortcut if it has one.

                A command that can't run is disabled, not hidden, and its
                tooltip says why: Build Spec is disabled until a project is
                open, and while the spec is building.

            height:
                The command area is the same height on every tab, even one with
                no commands, so the window beneath doesn't move when switching
                tabs.

            collapsing:
                The ribbon collapses to only its tabs, and expands again, with
                a chevron button at the right end of the tab bar, by
                double-clicking a tab, or with Ctrl+F1 (Cmd+F1 on macOS).
                Clicking a tab while the ribbon is collapsed selects it and
                expands the ribbon. Whether it is collapsed is saved for the
                user and restored on the next launch.
'''),
]
for a,b in pairs:
    assert s.count(a)==1,a[:50]; s=s.replace(a,b)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
piton check $(find spec -name '*.pi') 2>&1 | tail -6; piton build check 2>&1 | tail -3

content.text:
You're right: the spec had no ribbon at all. `MainWindow.pi` still described the old toolbar. I replaced that section with a full ribbon description, including the group titles. `piton check` and `piton build check` both pass.

It now says:
- **Tabs:** Project, Code, Spec, Research and Application, using gpui-kit's Tab component with default styling, and the window always opens on Project.
- **Groups:** each group has a small, muted title centred along its bottom, with a thin divider between groups.
  - Project has a "Project" group with Open Project.
  - Spec has a "Build" group with Build Spec.
  - Application has an "Appearance" group with the Dark mode switch and a "Preferences" group with Settings.
  - Code and Research read "No commands yet".
- **Commands:**
  - Large icons above labels, and on/off settings are switches.
  - Tooltips explain what a command does and show its shortcut.
  - Build Spec is disabled rather than hidden when it can't run, with the reason in its tooltip.
- **Height:** every tab has the same height.
- **Collapsing:** the chevron, double-clicking a tab, or Ctrl/Cmd+F1, and it's remembered across launches.

I also updated the dark mode section, which said the switch was at the far right of the toolbar.

Two gaps remain:
- **Settings window:** the spec mentions it but never describes it. That covers the editable system prompts, `.suspense/system-prompts` and Ctrl+,.
- **Palette:** its System tab still lists "Build", while the app now says "Build Spec" (`spec/scope/palette/index.pi`).
